action: Record the answers so the next return reuses them.

action: Report the choice and its reasons to the data governance board.

action: Include data protection terms from the procurement policy note.

action: Review alongside DQAP results each quarter.

action: Hand over the DQAP, quality rules, runbook and open issues.

title: Hand over to business as usual
action: Use the ownership model's transition steps and set the next review date.

action: Put data duties into role descriptions and objectives.

action: Train each role at the right level and give stewards protected time.

title: Plan people change, not just process change
action: Communicate why the policy matters in terms of services and people, not compliance.

title: Show the benefits
action: Agree a few measures before starting, such as reuse requests met, duplicate collections stopped or time spent cleansing.

title: Show the benefits
action: Take a baseline, then measure each year with the return.

title: Show the benefits
action: Use proportionate evaluation methods.

title: Keep the yearly cycle running in business as usual
action: Set fixed dates for asset review, metadata updates, DQAP review and the board.

title: Keep the yearly cycle running in business as usual
action: Track each owner's actions between returns.

title: Keep the yearly cycle running in business as usual
action: Feed lessons into the next year's priorities.

action: Run the government data maturity assessment or use the self-assessment here as a first pass.

action: Set a target level for each DAM strand with dates.

action: Repeat every one to two years.

action: Prefer open standards and APIs that follow the government API standards.

action: Record each system's exit route against its assets in the catalogue.

action: Test restoring an asset and check its quality afterwards against the DQAP rules.

title: Prepare for a cyber incident affecting a critical asset
action: Agree who tells data users when an asset may be affected.
